_comment: TXN_DATE_TIME formats in the forecast-balance source, and the wall-clock precision each one carries. Separate from date_formats.json, which describes the v4 workbook: that file writes '/' as day-first with 0 counterexamples, this one mixes both conventions in the same column (10814 rows provably day-first, 44902 provably month-first), so the two vocabularies cannot be merged without one of them losing. 'precision' is the finest unit the format can express, which is what stops a rendered 00:00:00 from being read as an observed midnight.

zone.name: Asia/Beirut
zone._comment: The source clock, established from the epoch column: 8142 of its values decode to exactly 21:00 or 22:00 UTC, and the split between them moves on the last Sunday of March and October in all four years covered. That is EET/EEST. The offset is identical across all 12 merchant countries, so it is the processor's clock rather than the merchant's local time. Athens or Helsinki would give byte-identical results; the label is Beirut because LB is 65% of rows. Applied ONLY to the epoch column -- every other format is already a wall-clock reading and is never shifted.

_null_token_comment: Date-shaped values that mean 'no date'. 9999-12-31 is the one that has to be listed rather than discovered: it appears in 353 SETTLE_DATE rows as a far-future 'never settled' sentinel, and it is outside the bounds of a nanosecond timestamp, so parsing it raises rather than producing a wrong answer. 0000-00-00 covers another 543. Both become NaT and are counted; MissingValueHandler is what turns that null into a status.
